Pascal’s law states that pressure applied to an enclosed fluid is transmitted undiminished to every part of the fluid and to the walls of its container. A hydraulic press is an application.
Elasticity is the property of a solid by which it returns to its original shape and size when the deforming force is removed.

Hooke’s law states that, within the elastic limit, extension is directly proportional to the applied force. Beyond the elastic limit, an object does not fully return to its original shape and size when the force is removed.
Force is a push or pull, measured in newtons. Pressure is force per unit area, measured in pascals.
For a liquid of fixed density, pressure is directly proportional to depth: p = ρgh.

Hooke’s law states that, within the elastic limit, extension is directly proportional to applied force. Applications include spring balances, suspension springs and weighing machines.

A mercury barometer measures atmospheric pressure: atmospheric pressure on the mercury reservoir supports a column in an inverted, closed-end tube, and the column height indicates the pressure. A manometer measures gas pressure by the difference in liquid levels in its limbs; it is used, for example, to measure pressure in a gas vessel or pipe.

Pascal’s law states that pressure applied to an enclosed fluid is transmitted undiminished throughout the fluid and to the container walls. Applications include hydraulic presses, hydraulic lifts and automobile brakes.
Liquid pressure depends on the liquid’s density, the depth and gravitational acceleration. It is determined by p = ρgh.
The weight of the air above Earth’s surface produces atmospheric pressure. Examples of its applications include drinking through a straw, using a syringe and using a suction cup.
